requirements.requirement: Establish filesystem snapshot capability for /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: No LVM/btrfs/spare device existed; executor installed btrfs-progs, created a loop-backed btrfs image, mounted a 'data' subvolume at /srv/data, and persisted the mount via /etc/fstab. Confirmed present and correctly mounted both before and after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Capture a snapshot of /srv/data before modification
requirements.summary: Populated /srv/data with sample files, recorded SHA-256 checksums, then took a read-only btrfs snapshot ('snap-baseline') of the data subvolume.

requirements.requirement: Modify /srv/data after the snapshot was taken
requirements.summary: Edited app.conf and accounts.csv, deleted logs/app.log, and added an unauthorized logs/tampered.log; checksum diff confirmed the divergence from baseline.

requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/data to the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: Deleted the modified 'data' subvolume, recreated it as a writable snapshot of 'snap-baseline', remounted at /srv/data, and verified byte-for-byte via SHA-256 checksum diff against the baseline (zero difference); confirmed tampered.log absent and app.log restored.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: it established btrfs-based snapshot capability for /srv/data on node1 (via a loop-mounted image since no snapshot-capable filesystem existed), captured a baseline read-only snapshot, modified the directory, and restored the exact baseline content, verified byte-for-byte via SHA-256 checksums. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity post-reboot, and full recovery of mounts, subvolumes, and data checksums, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The only blemish is a handful of leftover diagnostic log/checksum files left in /tmp, a minor and low-risk hygiene issue.
limitations: Restoration and restart were only exercised once each; multiple restore/reboot cycles were not tested, though the single demonstrated cycle is directly and completely evidenced.
Minor /tmp residue (log and checksum files) was not cleaned up after verification, though this does not affect functional correctness.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor state-changing commands trace clearly to the task (btrfs setup, fstab persistence, data population/modification/restoration, and the mandated restart protocol). The mandatory single-node restart was properly evidenced: pre-restart boot_id (45805187-...) and healthy checksums, a reboot acknowledgement, repeated connection resets/timeouts consistent with an actual reboot, a changed post-restart boot_id (6e850278-...) with uptime 0, and post-restart confirmation that mounts, subvolumes, and file checksums matched baseline exactly — independently corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity before/after-executor observations. The only minor issue is residue: several diagnostic files (apk-install.log, mkfs.log, baseline/modified/restored/postrestart-checksum.txt, reboot.log) were left under /tmp and not cleaned up after verification, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff. This is low-risk, non-destructive residue rather than a security or availability concern.
